name: Spanish nationalism
summary: Spanish nationalism holds that Spain is a single, indivisible nation and defends the unity of its state against Catalan, Basque and other peripheral nationalisms. It has liberal, Catholic-conservative, regenerationist and Francoist forms, and today runs from constitutional unionism to Vox's call for a unitary state, with Catholic tradition, the monarchy, Castilian and Hispanic cultural ties as recurring themes.
scope: The contemporary mainstream of españolismo: defence of the indissoluble unity of the Spanish nation under the 1978 constitution and monarchy, with its harder edge as put by Vox (abolish autonomies, restrictive immigration, Catholic family values). Historical National-Catholic, Falangist and Hispanidad strands (Menéndez Pelayo, Maeztu, José Antonio Primo de Rivera, Franco) are drawn on where they define the tradition, and answers on authoritarian questions treat these as a minority strand today. Excludes Catalan, Basque and Galician nationalisms.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Public healthcare is accepted across the Spanish right; Vox proposes a single national medical card and recentralised health management rather than dismantling it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Vox is described as economically liberal, though with protectionist elements, so adherents lean pro-market without the claim being central to the nationalism.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents are split: Vox is deregulatory in tax and labour terms but protective of national companies.

cut-welfare.rationale: Vox favours pronatalist family support and spending cuts at regional level rather than welfare cuts as such, so adherents lean against the claim of dependency.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Vox rejects hate-speech and gender-ideology laws as speech restrictions, though it also supports banning separatist parties.

strong-leader.rationale: Francoist and Falangist strands exalted a strong leader, while the constitutional mainstream of today does not; adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: Spanish nationalism is a justification of a centralised Spanish state, so denying the state's necessity contradicts its core.

limit-guns.rationale: Vox backs the castle doctrine but explicitly not a right to carry arms, so strict limits fit the platform.

empower-police-military.rationale: Vox calls for law-and-order policies, longer sentences and stronger defence, security and frontiers.

decide-locally.rationale: Vox wants to abolish the autonomous communities, but the constitutional mainstream accepts the State of Autonomies and Article 2 guarantees self-government of nationalities and regions, so the centralising lean is mild.

rehabilitation.rationale: Vox advocates longer sentences for violent crimes and life sentences for sexual offenders, favouring punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Vox defends traditional family values and natalism, and National-Catholicism made the Catholic family a keystone.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Vox opposes same-sex marriage while supporting civil unions; the centre-right mainstream is divided, so only a mild disagree.

abortion-legal.rationale: Vox opposes abortion and Catholicism was central to the Francoist strand.

more-religion-public.rationale: National-Catholicism made Catholic unity a pillar of the nation, and Vox defends Catholicism, though the constitution gives no state religion.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Vox opposes what it calls gender ideology.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending the unity and traditions of the Spanish nation is the defining aim of Spanish nationalism, including Catholic and Castilian cultural heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Liberal and conservative strands stress institutions and the 1978 settlement; the Francoist and Falangist strands were more radical, so only a mild answer.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Vox calls for deporting illegal immigrants and stricter citizenship rules, and is highly critical of multiculturalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.

reviewHistory.rationale: Vox is Eurosceptic and wants to leave the WHO, favouring national sovereignty over international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Vox mixes economic liberalism with protectionist elements favouring national companies, so adherents are split.

nation-first.rationale: Vox's programme foregrounds Spanish unity and sovereignty and is Eurosceptic and critical of supranational limits.

open-borders.rationale: Vox demands border defence and deportation, which is directly opposed to open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Vox opposes mainstream environmental policy and has moved only from climate denial to a conservationist stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources give no position; Vox backs nuclear energy but technological optimism is not a nationalist theme.

revolution-justified.rationale: The mainstream stands on the constitutional order that armed forces are charged to uphold; revolution is rejected, though the 1936 uprising is a historical complication.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Vox has protectionist elements favouring national companies.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Francoist strand directed industry through the state while the modern right is liberal; adherents are split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Falangist and Francoist strands built state-run vertical syndicates, but modern adherents do not; split by strand.

one-party-rule.rationale: Francoism used a single party, but today's adherents work within a parliamentary monarchy with political pluralism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The constitution makes the King head of state and symbol of Spanish unity, and Vox supports the constitutional monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Contemporary Spanish nationalists operate within and defend the 1978 democratic constitution, though the Francoist strand did not.

workers-councils.rationale: Contradicts the constitutional parliamentary order that Spanish nationalism defends.

right-to-secede.rationale: Article 2 rests the constitution on the indissoluble unity of the Spanish nation, and Vox wants separatist parties banned.

natural-rulers.rationale: Constitutional Spanish nationalism rests on popular sovereignty; elitist claims belong to older reactionary strands.

political-violence-never.rationale: Contemporary adherents condemn separatist and terrorist violence, but the Francoist origin in a military uprising complicates this.

war-builds-character.rationale: Military ethos is strong in the Francoist and Falangist strands, but the modern mainstream does not hold this.

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 16 requires cooperation with the Catholic Church, and National-Catholicism tied the nation to the faith.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Hispanidad links the nation to Catholicism as culture and identity, but Spain's constitution forbids a state religion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The armed forces' constitutional task is to defend Spain's sovereignty and territorial integrity, which sits with the state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Spanish nationalism defines the nation by culture, Catholicism and language, and Maeztu's Hispanidad is a community across races, so it is not mainly ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation, not class, as the main unit, and the Falange rejected Marxism.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Hispanidad presents Spanish America as Spain's work and a spiritual community, so adherents reject reparations framing.

civilizational-union.rationale: Hispanidad is a community of Spain and former colonies through language and Catholicism, though it is mostly cultural, not political.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Catholic and communitarian emphasis on duty works against celebrating self-interest, though the economic liberals differ.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Hispanidad-inflected and National-Catholic thought stresses duty to nation and faith over individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Vox has moved toward a conservationist stance but not toward intrinsic value; no clear position.

limit-population.rationale: Vox promotes natalism and opposes limiting births.

restore-past-order.rationale: Reactionary and Hispanidad-inflected thought looks back to Catholic imperial Spain, but liberal strands do not.

direct-action.rationale: Spanish nationalism defends the constitutional order and parliament, and condemns unlawful action by separatists.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist principle foreign to Spanish nationalism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist claim rejected by a nationalist right with a pro-business, lower-tax platform.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Francoism and the Falange defined themselves against communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist-Leninist thesis foreign to Spanish nationalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Vox seeks lower taxes but treats the state as necessary, so the strong claim is rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: Vox defends traditional morality and restricts abortion and euthanasia on moral grounds.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The nationalism asserts a collective national subject whose unity is indivisible, so rights are not purely individual.

positive-liberty.rationale: Catholic social thought and the Falange endorsed social provision but modern liberals do not; split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Hispanidad stresses a community of faith across races, and modern adherents reject racial hierarchy, though Francoist eugenics existed.

organic-representation.rationale: Francoist organic democracy used family, municipality and syndicate, while Vox seeks equal-weight votes; split.

total-state.rationale: Falangism approached this but the modern mainstream does not, and the constitution protects pluralism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Regenerationism and Falangism framed Spain as needing renewal after decline, and Vox speaks of a Spain to be revived.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Falange spoke of empire, but contemporary adherents do not seek expansion; Gibraltar claims are separate.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contradicts the constitutional order of sovereignty, law and monarchy that adherents defend.

bound-labor.rationale: Contradicts modern constitutional, liberal and Catholic social positions.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Hispanidad opposed rationalism, but a relativist claim that knowledge reflects power is a left-postmodern thesis.

single-common-good.rationale: Catholic and Falangist thinking holds a single common good of the nation above party interest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Vox is pro-Israel in international orientation, although the sources do not give the exact position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Adherents treat Castilian as the common language and tend to resist revival or promotion of regional languages.

school-vouchers.rationale: Vox supports parental rights in education through the pin parental.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Vox advocates spending cuts and lower taxes.

economic-freedom.rationale: Vox is described as economically liberal.

national-self-determination.rationale: Spanish nationalism holds that only the Spanish nation is sovereign and rejects Catalan or Basque self-determination.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Maeztu's Hispanidad rejected rationalism and liberalism for Catholic values.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Falange and National-Catholicism favoured class collaboration within the nation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Spanish nationalism defends inherited national culture and history.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism places workers within the nation rather than an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Vox opposes gender ideology but does not propose legal role distinctions; split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Hispanidad stresses community across races; segregation has no place in the nationalism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist claim rejected by the nationalist right.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Vox opposes mainstream environmental policy though it supports nuclear energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Vox is highly critical of multiculturalism and prefers Hispanic American immigrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some on the hard edge allude to replacement, but the typical adherent does not state it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Vox wants electoral reform so every vote carries equal weight, though it is not committed to full proportionality.

national-mission.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale describes a mission that is not about spreading a form of government (religious, cultural, racial, imperial or leadership), and the statement now asks whether the country should treat spreading its form of government abroad as a special national mission.

reviewHistory.rationale: Hispanidad presents a spiritual mission of Spain toward Hispanic America, though modern adherents are less missionary.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Vox opposes feminist structural analyses and gender violence law.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Vox's populist posture criticises the political class and calls for cutting political spending.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Francoist eugenics existed historically, but contemporary adherents do not hold it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Vox seeks to repeal the Historical Memory Law and opposes Franco's exhumation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Vox backs family policy and national services, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hispanidad celebrates the mestizo Hispanic world, so discouraging mixture is rejected.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Maeztu's racial egalitarianism applied to salvation, and the constitution protects equality, but Spanish nationalism is not centrally about this.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Hispanidad regards the Spanish colonial legacy as a civilising community, rejecting the colonial label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Centralist Spanish nationalism favours equal national law over regional or foral variation; religion-specific codes are not at issue.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article 16 guarantees freedom of religion, and the nationalism is Catholic more than coercive.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an issue in Spanish nationalism; Vox defends traditional meat culture.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Vox backs parental choice and Catholic heritage in schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not shared by Spanish nationalists.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The constitution places national sovereignty in the Spanish people, though adherents locate the people in the whole of Spain.

population-transfer.rationale: Vox targets illegal immigrants and offending foreigners, not the removal of resident minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Adherents accept state force to defend territorial integrity, so an absolute rule is not held.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Catholic and communitarian thinking differs from social-Darwinist framing, though liberals disagree.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Vox wants separatist parties banned, while the mainstream allows parties to argue for secession peacefully and the 2002 parties law targets support for terrorism rather than aims.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1978 constitution adheres to a division of powers which adherents defend, though Vox seeks reform.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine opposed by Spanish nationalism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social thinking supports it, while the liberal right prioritises other things; split.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Vox is highly critical of multiculturalism and defends a single national identity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inconsistent with the constitutional order of election and monarchy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Vox calls for suspending Catalan self-government, implying broad emergency powers, though ordinary rights suspension is not specified.

party-controls-media.rationale: Spanish nationalists today operate under a constitution protecting pluralism; Francoist controls are not endorsed.

party-commands-army.rationale: Article 8 gives the army to the constitutional state and the King commands it nominally.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Vox calls for cutting political spending but does not call for pay parity.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Vox is Eurosceptic and sits in Patriots for Europe.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The constitutional King's acts require countersignature and the government directs the forces; this model is rejected.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic doctrine is governed by bishops, and National-Catholicism accepts this.

clerical-rule.rationale: Article 16 says no religion shall have state character.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Spanish nationalism is patriotic and wishes national victory.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Francoism censored for Catholic morality but modern adherents mostly defend speech and tradition; split.

people-in-arms.rationale: Vox backs professional military and security forces, and opposes a right to carry arms.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not directly addressed; Gibraltar is a separate territorial claim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist elements exist but no clear position in sources.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hispanidad treats Catholic Hispanic civilisation as a distinct ideal, not as one among equals.

death-penalty.rationale: Vox favours life sentences and long terms rather than execution, and the constitution abolishes it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Vox's pin parental and rejection of gender ideology oppose such curricula.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Vox seeks stricter citizenship rules and prefers Hispanic ties.

minority-language-support.rationale: Spanish law has favoured Castilian, and centralist adherents resist regional-language promotion.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Catholic traditionalism values custom over eccentricity.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not an issue for Spanish nationalists.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Adherents defend the 1978 constitution; rewriting by assembly is not favoured.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The constitution makes the King head of state and adherents defend this.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Catholic social doctrine and Falangism limited property to social function.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Adherents saw the Soviet Union as a communist tyranny, not a variant of capitalism.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Article 56 defines the King as symbol of unity and permanence, arbitrating institutions.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 8 gives the army the task of defending territorial integrity, and Vox seeks to suspend Catalan self-government.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: Spanish nationalism rejects special regimes that weaken unity, though the constitution does recognise foral rights.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The monarchy is constitutional and the King inviolable, not sacred or divine.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Vox proposes a simplified income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Catholic thinking allows nature and free will, and nationalism holds an enduring national character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The constitutional monarchy is bound by law and countersignature.

leader-cult.rationale: Francoism had a leader cult, but modern constitutional adherents do not endorse it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question; adherents reject the premises.

refugee-return.rationale: Spanish nationalism has no documented position on refugee return, and adherents' views on forced displacement vary, so neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Contemporary adherents do not claim territory on this basis.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Article 16 guarantees religious freedom, which adherents accept.

women-must-cover.rationale: Vox is critical of Islam and multiculturalism, and Spanish nationalism is Western and Catholic.

common-currency.rationale: Vox is Eurosceptic and favours national sovereignty, so adherents lean against shared currencies, though Spain's mainstream right accepts the euro.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Hispanidad is a spiritual community, not a political union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Spanish nationalism holds the nation indivisible and resists such autonomy for Catalan and Basque institutions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist thesis opposed to nationalism and Catholic idealism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not a nationalist theme; Vox's liberal and protectionist strands point in opposite directions, so neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Adherents rely on constitutional courts to block secession referendums and regional measures.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Vox opposes gender quotas and gender-ideology legislation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Francoist autarky is historical; modern adherents are not autarkic.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not a Spanish nationalist theme; the Falange stressed service but modern adherents are market-liberal.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Rejected as separatist or Marxist terrorism by adherents.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Vox seeks to recentralise education, and Spanish nationalism emphasises Spanish identity and heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hispanidad rhetoric had a civilising mission, but contemporary adherents disavow it.

patriotic-education.rationale: Vox wants recentralised education and promotes national symbols; Spanish nationalism features the flag prominently.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Hispanidad and Francoist policy built a Council and Institute of Hispanic culture to cultivate ties to Latin America.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist thesis not held by adherents.

elective-rulers.rationale: Adherents defend the hereditary monarchy as head of state.

minority-veto.rationale: Adherents reject regional vetoes against national decisions.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The constitution makes the Cortes the lawmaker, within constitutional limits.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Vox defends bullfighting but has no explicit stance on sentience.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Vox defends hunting and traditional animal practices.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Catholic social tradition and the Falange stressed obligations of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nationalism calls for civic commitment to the nation.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis, opposed by adherents.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim not held by adherents.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is outside Spanish nationalism's concerns; the sources give no basis for a lean.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Spanish nationalism claims Gibraltar; the sources only touch territorial integrity.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Vox is described as revisionist toward Francoism and opposes Franco's exhumation.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The mainstream right accepts this, while the Francoist heritage rejects the equivalence; split.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Vox opposes Franco's exhumation and seeks to repeal the Historical Memory Law.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Vox wants to replace the gender violence law with a family violence law.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Vox wants to replace the gender violence law with a broader family violence law.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Hispanidad rejects liberal rationalism but adherents also defend Western democracy; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Article 8 tasks the army to uphold the constitutional order; historical Francoism went further.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Vox has protectionist elements favouring national companies.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Inconsistent with the representative parliamentary order.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary monarchy requires budget approval; adherents accept this.

single-official-language.rationale: Article 3 makes Castilian the official language of the State, and centralist adherents want it to dominate public life.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Catholic traditionalism critiques it but the liberal right does not; split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Vox promotes natalism through family support.

residents-only-property.rationale: Centralist nationalism opposes local restrictions that treat Spaniards differently by region.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents defend the legal and constitutional order.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereigntist adherents favour non-interference, but Atlanticist ones accept NATO action; the sources do not decide, so neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Vox rejects far-right labels; modern adherents do not advance such conspiracy claims, though Francoist rhetoric did.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Vox's programme has an electoral law and transparency section.

religious-nation.rationale: National-Catholicism defined the nation by faith, while modern constitutional adherents do not; split.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Centralist adherents reject claims of fiscal drainage and want pooled national revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: Adherents defend private property of means of production too.

defeat-communism.rationale: Francoism was explicitly anti-communist and Vox opposes the left.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Vox wants to recentralise services without a stated view on provider mix; adherents are split between liberal and statist views.

religion-illusion.rationale: Catholicism is central to National-Catholicism and Hispanidad.

socialized-care.rationale: Vox favours the traditional family as the base of care.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not a stated Spanish nationalist policy.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Spanish nationalism uses Reconquista and historical unity of the nation as legitimacy.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of Spanish nationalism and Vox is pro-Israel.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Adherents want separatist parties banned, but accept pluralism otherwise.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Hispanidad speaks of shared community, not exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not applicable; Vox is hostile to Islamism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Adherents accept constitutional rule and no state religion.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Vox rejects far-right labels but not the left-right divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist claim not held by adherents.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The Reconquista narrative defined Spain against Islam, and Vox is critical of multiculturalism and prefers Hispanic immigration.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The constitution places sovereignty in the people, though the Francoist strand claimed divine grounding.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Vox is critical of Islam and multiculturalism, but the sources give no stated rule on religious dress in state institutions, so neutral.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment law on nondisclosure agreements is outside Spanish nationalism's documented concerns, so neutral.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Article 8 gives the armed forces a constitutional mission.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a constitutional or ceremonial crown, and the statement now asks only about passing real governing power to a child.

reviewHistory.rationale: The constitution is a hereditary monarchy and adherents defend it.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a constitutional or ceremonial crown, and the statement now asks only about passing real governing power to a child.

property-franchise.rationale: The constitution has universal suffrage and adherents accept it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist idea opposed by adherents.

reification.rationale: A Marxist thesis not held by adherents.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Constitutional rule of law is accepted by adherents.

racial-franchise.rationale: Contradicts universal national citizenship under the constitution.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Adherents accept the constitutional order, which guarantees religious freedom.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Adherents are pro-market and do not stress it.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Spain permits this already and the sources record no nationalist campaign against it, though Vox's social conservatism pulls the other way.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Catholicism is central to the nationalism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Vox backs law and order and longer sentences.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Spanish nationalism opposes plurinational power-sharing and holds the Spanish nation single.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Catholic charity and liberal views split from welfare statist views.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Catholic doctrine reserves priesthood to men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The constitution establishes equality of spouses, which adherents accept.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Francoist Frente de Juventudes did this, but modern adherents do not.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Vox supports nuclear energy but the sources give no view on nuclear weapons; Spanish adherents are split between Atlanticists and sovereigntists.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Falangist and Catholic social thought favoured wide ownership, while Vox's liberal economics does not stress it; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The constitution gives the armed forces the task of defending Spain, and nationalists accept lethal force in defence of nation and person.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Spanish nationalism, from Menendez Pelayo to Vox, presents Spain as a nation continuous from Visigothic and medieval Reconquista origins.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Article 2 stresses the indissoluble unity of Spain and nationalists oppose merging regions such as Catalonia, Valencia and Navarre into peoples' units.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Adherents are split between Vox's liberalising line and the Catholic-conservative tradition of public welfare.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1978 Constitution, the mainstream's reference, sets up a Senate alongside the Congress of Deputies.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The tradition defends the indivisible nation and Vox wants a unitary state, so confederations of self-governing towns run against it.

person-over-state.rationale: The 1978 Constitution, central to mainstream Spanish nationalism, grounds the order on the dignity of the person and inviolable rights.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Catholic tradition and Hispanidad are recurring themes, though the mainstream is constitutional and secular in form.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Vox calls for a unitary state and abolition of the autonomies, and the mainstream holds the nation indivisible, so regional powers rest on national authority.

racial-pride.rationale: Hispanidad stresses cultural and historical pride, not race; adherents are not committed either way.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The constitution assigns the armed forces the defence of Spain's sovereignty and integrity, and no tradition stresses wars of choice.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Spanish nationalism holds Spain is one indissoluble nation containing several languages, so it denies that a shared language (Catalan, Basque) makes a separate nation.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not an issue in the sources; adherents are split between constitutional transparency and defence of state confidentiality.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Defence of national unity and the armed forces is central to españolismo, which treats the army as guarantor of the nation.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Adherents are split between Vox-style market preferences and the mainstream right's acceptance of Spain's existing collective agreements.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The 2011 reform of the constitution (Article 135) enshrined budgetary stability and debt limits, backed by the Spanish right.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Spanish nationalists defend the constitution, the monarchy and the existing state, and seek to preserve rather than destroy it.

sacred-nation.rationale: Spanish nationalism treats Spain as an indivisible, historic nation with Catholic and Hispanic roots that outlasts individuals.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Spanish nationalists reject the Catalan and Basque claim that Spain plunders their regions and treat it as separatist propaganda.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 1978 Constitution, which this strand defends, guarantees equality before the law (art. 14) and the right to private property and inheritance (art. 33).

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The Constitution makes Castilian the official language that all Spaniards must know (art. 3), and Vox demands assimilation and a restrictive immigration policy.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1978 constitution keeps cooperation with the Catholic Church and the tradition treats Catholicism as central to Spanish identity, so equal treatment is only weakly held.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The 1978 constitution sets competitive elections as the basis of legitimacy and the mainstream movement defends that order.

premarital-sex.rationale: Mainstream españolismo accepts sexual freedom in practice while its Catholic-conservative strand disapproves; adherents are split.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1978 constitution guarantees equality and equal political participation for women and the movement defends it.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Vox opposes equality ministries and gender-violence agencies, while mainstream unionists accept them; the hard edge sets the answer.

national-church-status.rationale: The constitution (art. 16.3) singles out the Catholic Church for cooperation, and the National-Catholic and Vox strands want Catholic tradition privileged.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The constitution recognises regional autonomy but rests on the indissoluble unity of the nation, and Vox would abolish the autonomies; ethnic-majority autonomy as such is resisted.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The movement rejects self-determination votes, as in Catalonia, and Spain refuses to let Gibraltarians decide the Rock's sovereignty.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription was suspended in 2001 and the sources do not show a settled adherent position on its gender terms.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Spanish nationalism, especially Hispanidad and Vox, treats Spain as an ancestral patria whose heritage is to be guarded, though the stress is on unity and tradition rather than a spiritual tie to land.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Hispanidad extends Spanish identity to the Spanish-speaking world, and the 1978 constitution commits the state to protect Spaniards abroad, though kin minorities in neighbouring countries are not a central theme.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Mainstream españolismo works through parties and the constitutional monarchy, and Vox is a party; the leader-direct-to-people idea belongs to the Falangist minority strand.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Hispanidad and Vox couple modern economy with traditional Catholic and Spanish values, a combination the sources describe as their programme.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Spanish nationalists defend legality under the constitution against Catalan secession attempts and treat laws as binding until changed.

multipolar-world.rationale: Hispanidad favours a Hispanic cultural sphere, but mainstream Spanish nationalism is Atlanticist and pro-EU, so adherents are split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The 1978 constitution establishes political pluralism and a market economy, and the strand opposes communist one-party rule.

police-more-powers.rationale: Vox calls for law-and-order policies, longer sentences and stronger defence, security and frontiers. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Vox favours pronatalist family support and spending cuts at regional level rather than welfare cuts as such, so adherents lean against the claim of dependency. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Hispanidad and Francoist policy built a Council and Institute of Hispanic culture to cultivate ties to Latin America. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A national government may suspend a region's self-government if its leaders act against the constitution.
missingStatements.rationale: Vox's programme opens with suspending Catalan self-government, and the constitutional unity article underlies the claim.

missingStatements.text: A country's regional governments should be abolished and replaced by a single centralised state.
missingStatements.rationale: Vox wants to abolish the autonomous communities and create a unitary state; centralism is the core of españolismo.

notes: Answers reflect the constitutional-unionist mainstream with Vox as the harder edge. Francoist and Falangist strands would answer authoritarian, corporatist, expansionist and eugenic items differently, so those are mostly 0 or low confidence.
